Transcript:
[00:00] Ariel (Redwood AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining on a wednesday afternoon, um i'll kick off  and keep it tight — today is mostly the security pulse for the oakridge pilot. Samir's on to handle the log / infra questions.
[00:18] Lena (Oakridge): thanks Ariel, appreciate it. We have a shorter agenda but a few blockers from security. Marcus is going to lead.
[00:26] Marcus (Oakridge Sec): yep hi all, quick context — we've got the POC running against Redwood hosted with prefix caching enabled, and we're seeing questions from our compliance team about audit log completeness and SAML attribute fidelity. Also want clarity on retention tiers.
[00:42] Samir (Redwood SE): got it. we looked at the audit pipeline last week — the platform emits event-level logs for every request, and there's also an admin-level audit trail for config / access changes. For the pilot we've got logs going to the hosted archive, but we can pull samples and show RBAC linkage.
[01:01] Evan (Oakridge Compliance): are those logs immutable? our policy requires write-once preservation for 90 days and tamper evidence for any alteration.
[01:12] Samir (Redwood SE): currently hosted retention is configurable; for immutable storage we integrate with customer-owned S3 and Object Lock via the Private product, but for hosted we can provide signed log exports and append-only streams with checksums. I will note that the append-only checksumming is not always presented in the same UI — it's more of an off-box export that we produce.
[01:33] Priya (Oakridge PM): wait can you repeat, Samir? when you say customer-owned S3, is that only for Redwood Private or Dedicated also supports that?
[01:44] Samir (Redwood SE): Dedicated supports VPC peering and can write to your S3 or to a dedicated bucket under redwood-managed tenancy, but if you need legal hold/object lock then Private with customer-managed S3 is the clearest path. Dedicated can be configured to replicate logs to your target as well, but the guarantee depends on the replication setup.
[02:05] Marcus: okay so for this pilot we are not ready to spin up Private. we want to prove the model and controls on hosted but still need exportable evidence that matches our SOC2 controls. can you produce that?
[02:18] Ariel: yes, that's common. we can produce time-stamped audit exports, access control mapping, and an artifacts bundle that shows role creation and permission changes for the pilot period. samir will produce a 48 hour sample with PII redacted.
[02:32] Marcus: redaction is key — we cannot move raw customer PII offsite. want to see sanitized records.
[02:40] Samir: understood. we'll obfuscate personal identifiers and provide the raw event schema as well.
[02:47] Lena: next item SSO — last week the IdP team sent metadata but they weren't clear on which attributes the product needs.
[02:58] Samir: for SAML we expect uid/email, name, groups, and optionally an "org_id" custom attribute for tenant mapping. sometimes the IdP uses mail or uid interchangeably which causes session mapping issues.
[03:12] Marcus: yep our IdP maps an "employeeNumber" attribute by default. can you accept custom attribute mappings?
[03:19] Samir: yes we support attribute remapping. in the console under enterprise > SSO there's a field for attribute mapping or we can do it server-side for pilot with a small transform. Note: metadata ingestion sometimes mis-labels the certificate fingerprint in the transcribe — the auto importer has had hiccups.
[03:36] Evan: and do you support SCIM for provisioning? we'd like user sync rather than manual invites.
[03:43] Ariel: SCIM is supported on enterprise tiers; for the pilot we can enable a limited SCIM connector so you can test deprovisioning flows.
[03:52] Priya: we also need to confirm session timeout defaults and org-wide RBAC roles — our security policy requires 15 minute idle time for elevated roles.
[04:02] Samir: session timeouts are configurable per org; we can surface the default in the console and enforce the 15m for admin roles. we'll capture the control in the artifacts bundle.
[04:16] [05:00 marker missing due to auto timestamps glitch — transcript continues]
[04:22] Marcus: another question — encryption at rest: do you use customer keys or platform keys? KMS integration?
[04:30] Samir: for hosted we use platform KMS; for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. There's also an option to bring your own key (BYOK) for Dedicated in some setups; depends on contract. We'll outline the options in the doc.
[04:46] Lena: perfect. SOC2 evidence, timeline wise — we need audit artifacts by the 28th because our internal audit window opens the 1st of november. is that reasonable?
[04:58] Ariel: possible. samir can produce the log export and the SSO mapping docs within two business weeks if we get the IdP metadata from you by next tuesday.
[05:10] Priya: we'll aim for 2026-10-20 to send the metadata.
[05:15] Samir: quick perf note — you asked last week about moving to Dedicated to get more predictable latency. we can spin up a tiny Dedicated pool for a short baseline. it takes ~10-14 days to provision but we can kick off the ordering once you sign the pilot change request. for benchmarking we'll run a small synthetic and a replay of 1k requests representative of your real load.
[05:40] Marcus: we do want to see the latency distribution especially at tail (p95/p99). hosted sometimes has bursts we want to understand.
[05:48] Samir: yeah we'll include p50/p95/p99 and token cost estimates. note that batching can change latency/cost tradeoff so we'll include both continuous batch and single-request modes.
[06:03] Ariel: one callout — we've seen customers ask about model fallback policies for compliance, e.g., if the primary model has an unknown license, fallback to a vetted open model. do you need that?
[06:14] Priya: interesting, our legal team is picky about model provenance. we need a list of certified models and their licenses.
[06:20] Samir: we have a model catalog; i'll export the curated list for pilot models and annotate license info. the catalog id sometimes gets mis-transcribed, so i'll also include direct model hash and version.
[06:33] Evan: on retention — we have three classes: short (30d), medium (90d), long (7 years) for legal holds. can the platform apply different retention to different event classes?
[06:46] Samir: yes, audit events, request payloads, and exports can be configured separately. for hosted, retention beyond 90d often requires an export to your object store or Private. We'll propose a retention architecture in the doc.
[06:58] Marcus: one more — how do you surface who viewed logs or ran queries? we need forensic trails.
[07:06] Samir: admin audit tracks console actions and log reads; we can show user_id, action, timestamp. For forensic needs we recommend pushing logs to your SIEM; we have integrations for Splunk/Datadog/ELK.
[07:20] Lena: can you show a sample Splunk ingestion pipeline? last time the schema wasn't lining up and the fields were nested oddly.
[07:28] Samir: i'll include a sample HEC mapping and a parsing guide, there was one mis-parse last week where a field named "k v cache" was tokenized weirdly by the exporter — we'll provide the exact key names.
[07:41] [08:00 timestamp gap — filler noise from auto system]
[07:48] Marcus: regarding encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS between customers and Dedicated nodes?
[07:55] Samir: yes for Private and Dedicated we support mTLS with client certs; hosted is TLS with certs managed by us. we can do VPN or peering for additional network separation.
[08:08] Priya: ok good. one item from legal — they want the chain of custody for training data if we ever need to debug hallucinations. can you provide lineage for model inputs/outputs while maintaining privacy?
[08:21] Samir: we keep request-level metadata and model version, but not full training corpora lineage. for debug we keep request/response hashes and the model snapshot id; we can also keep a retrace log with salted hashes to avoid exposing raw content.
[08:38] Evan: acceptable if the salted hashes and metadata are sufficient for reproducible debugging. we'll validate.
[08:44] Ariel: great, let's capture the concrete deliverables — samir will produce: 1) sanitized 48h audit log export, 2) SSO attribute mapping example + transformation steps, 3) retention architecture doc, 4) model catalog extract + license table, 5) sample Splunk HEC mapping.
[09:03] Samir: yes, and i'll upload to the shared pilot drive link and email a note.
[09:09] Priya: for the Dedicated baseline, we need the ordering checklist and expected lead time. Ariel?
[09:15] Ariel: i'll send a small change request and a pricing delta for a 4-week Dedicated baseline. Marcus, once you sign we'll start provisioning.
[09:23] Marcus: side question — competitors. we evaluated Anthropic and BigCloud AI, what would be the major differences from a controls perspective?
[09:32] Ariel: high level — vendors differ on default retention, BYOK options, and how they surface audit evidence. we'll include a short comparison table in the packet.
[09:41] Marcus: perfect.
[09:44] [Closing minutes: recap & next steps]
[09:46] Ariel: recap: oakridge to send IdP metadata by 10/20, samir to deliver log sample by 10/16, ariel to share pricing/ordering and SOC2 playbook by 10/18. we'll schedule the Dedicated baseline kickoff if you approve the change request. any objections?
[10:04] Lena: no objections. thanks everyone.
[10:07] Evan: quick note — please mark the artifacts with the audit ticket id we assign (AUD-331) so our audit team can pull them easily.
[10:15] Samir: will do.
[10:18] Ariel: thanks all, we'll follow up with links.
